subject: Using mirt for dichotomous item-response test

messages.author: 01bb6e9a8a9d9d33
messages.subject: Using mirt for dichotomous item-response test
parts:
Hello,

In our development of a CAT, we had originally adapted a typical 5-point Likert scale using a polytomous IRT model. However, we have recently decided to change this to a Yes/No dichotmous IRT model. This wouldn't normally be a problem, but most dichotmous IRT models assess Correct/Incorrect choices (e.g. "Is 2 + 2 = 4?), whereas our model assess Yes/No responses (e.g. "Are you able to walk?), which doesn't have a "correct" answer. Would approaching this design as a "two-item" polytomous model using mirt be applicable? This would only generate 1 B parameter per question. I am a bit confused as I rarely see a "two-item" Likert scale, and a Yes/No response isn't really ordinal. Any help would be appreciated, thank you.

messages.author: d0b18666fe8582cb
messages.subject: Re: Using mirt for dichotomous item-response test
parts:
You can think of the outcome you are modeling as the "yes" (or analogously the "correct") response. If your scale is modeling physical functioning ability, with higher scores indicating more physical functioning, then you can apply a 1PL or 2PL IRT model to these items, which are appropriate for dichotomous response categories. So in essence your IRT model would be estimating the probability of a "yes" response to each item given particular item characteristics (i.e., item difficulty if using a 1PL or both item difficulty and discrimination if using a 2PL)...

Keri
